Ana (sales): Heads-up — I just got asked by a large APAC prospect about the new rate card changes. They want to lock a 12-month commit but operate across eu-west and apac-south. The new APAC surcharge in v2026.3 is showing up in the quote and the AE is worried about churn during migration. Any guidance?

Mike (deal-desk): Do we have a formal grandfathering window for customers who sign before the public rollout? I remember a short grace period but not the exact rules.

Sophie - Pricing: Short answer: yes, there's a 90-day grandfathering window for committed SKUs if the contract is signed before the effective_date in the rate card. After that, new pricing applies. For APAC surcharges specifically, the surcharge is applied by region tag at invoice time, not baked into the SKU.

Ana (sales): Can we make an exception for this PoC-heavy deal? Customer will spike to 10x tokens for a month while doing evaluation. They asked for surcharge waiver for that month.

Tom E (revops): Exceptions allowed but require deal-desk approval + finance signoff. For short-term PoC spikes we usually offer a temporary credit instead of a permanent waiver. Example: we can credit the surcharge component for up to 30 days on invoice.

Mike (deal-desk): @Sophie — what's the right ticket to create for the finance approval? We need a clear wording so the AE can include it in the SOW.

Sophie - Pricing: Create a deal-exception ticket and tag with: "apac-surcharge-credit", customer name, commit term, expected spike window. Template text: "Grant one-time credit for regional surcharge (apac-south) covering evaluation period (30 days). Credit limited to surcharge amt only; base tokens billed. Requires finance approval."

Ana (sales): Copying that. One other question: if the AE signs them under current ratecard but we later make a global ratecard rollback (small decrease), do they automatically get the lower price?

Tom E (revops): No automatic downward adjustments. Grandfathering protects against increases only. If we decrease prices later, we can opt-in customers via a mass-apply patch, but it's not automatic per contract.

Mike (deal-desk): Ops note — make sure the quote has this clause: "Customer will be billed under Rate Card v2026.3 unless a lower rate card is explicitly applied in writing by Redwood Inference." Saves future confusion.

Ana (sales): Thanks. Last nit: the AE asked about using a temporary promo code in the quoting tool to reflect the credit. Is that supported?

Sophie - Pricing: Yes — use promo code "APAC-CREDIT-30" in the quoting UI. It only applies to line items flagged as regional surcharge; it does not touch committed token rates. I'll leave the promo active for 72 hours after approval.

ops-bot: deploy-notice: Ratecard v2026.3 scheduled public rollout 2026-06-18 16:00 UTC. Grandfathering window applies to contracts signed before rollout.

Ana (sales): Perfect — I'll proceed and open the deal-exception ticket with the exact wording. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

Mike (deal-desk): If you post the ticket link here I’ll route to finance immediately.

Sophie - Pricing: Also adding a short FAQ blurb to the internal Rate Card doc about region surcharges and promo flow. Will ping when done.

Ana (sales): Link to ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/DE-4821 — created and tagged.

Tom E (revops): Got it, routed to finance. Expect approval in ~24-48h unless they ask for more detail.

Ana (sales): Great, closing the loop — will update the AE once finance signs off.
